seo.title: What is responsive design?
seo.description: Responsive design means one website that rearranges itself to work on any screen, from a phone to a wide monitor.

definition: Responsive design means one website that rearranges itself to work on any screen, from a phone to a wide monitor.
answerBlock: Responsive design means one website that rearranges itself to work on any screen, from a phone to a wide monitor. There is no separate mobile site to maintain and no horizontal scrolling. The layout, the type and the images all adapt to the space available.

body.heading: What separates responsive from merely shrunk?
paragraphs: A shrunken desktop layout keeps its desktop assumptions: tables that overflow, tap targets sized for a mouse, images downloaded at full size on a phone connection. Responsive design changes the arrangement, not just the scale.

The details that matter are unglamorous. Content sits inside a gutter at every width. Rows wrap or stack rather than squeezing. Tables and diagrams get their own scrolling container so the page itself never scrolls sideways. Images are served at a size that suits the screen.
Touch targets are part of it: controls need to be large enough and far enough apart to hit accurately, which WCAG 2.2 makes an explicit criterion.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: Most B2B research now starts on a phone even when the purchase is signed on a desktop. A site that is awkward on a phone loses buyers at the first step of the process.
One responsive site is also cheaper to run than a desktop site plus a mobile variant that slowly falls out of date.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: Meridian Parts built fitment search for a technician holding a phone in a workshop, which is a harder target than a buyer at a desk and a better one to design for.

service.title: Custom website development
service.line: Research-led design built around how your buyers actually decide, not around a template's section order.

terms.definition: Accessibility means a website can be used by people with disabilities, and WCAG is the published standard that defines what that requires.
A design system is the agreed set of colours, type, spacing and components that every page of a product is built from.
Information architecture is how a site is organised: what pages exist, how they are grouped, and what each one is called.
A wireframe is a deliberately plain layout of a page that settles what is on it and in what order, before anyone decides how it looks.
